notes: Board of Park Commissioners minutes, April 1913 - December 1916, a typed volume. Curated: buildings, gifts, transfers and the Church Street railway.

coverage.remaining: Supply bids and routine items not curated. Not placed: the Clarke memorial gateway at the Arguello Boulevard entrance to Golden Gate Park by Bliss & Faville (plans approved December 1, 1914; no page), the convenience station at 10th Avenue and Fulton (Reid Bros.), the Broderick and Baker statues for the Civic Center, the White Pine Building and the Virginia Building proposed for Lincoln Park, 'The End of the Trail' proposed for the Lincoln Highway terminus.
coverage.note: Dated by the meeting opener ('Golden Gate Park, Thursday, <date>') or the 'San Francisco, <date>' heading; the volume interleaves special meetings out of order. Curated list PB1913.py.

findings.address_as_written: Communication from M. Hagiwara re Japanese Temple
findings.description: M. Hagiwara, who held the Japanese Tea Garden in Golden Gate Park, asked the Board of Park Commissioners for permission to put up a real Japanese temple in the proposed new tea garden, its site subject to the board's approval; the board left it to Superintendent McLaren with full power to act.

findings.address_as_written: Re. Municipal R.R. - Church Street Railway through Mission Park
findings.description: After a hearing at which neighbors argued Mission Park had been dedicated for park purposes only, the Board of Park Commissioners granted the Board of Public Works' request to run the Church Street municipal railway through the westerly end of Mission Park, to avoid Church Street's steep grades, and confirmed the grant on September 16, 1915 once the City Attorney advised that it had the power.
